newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - July 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - July 10.

text.p: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL said that, faced with so many urgent issues, Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa apparently wanted to resolve problems quickly and had neglected the rule of law. The paper said it supported the government's stance against illegal immigration, but added that deporting its own citizens was not the act of a civilised government.

-- APPLE DAILY said the provisional legislature's performance on Wednesday showed that it was just acting like a rubber stamp. The paper said how the courts handled challenges to the bill curbing child illegal immigration would decide in what direction the rule of law in Hong Kong was going.

-- The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO supported the government's move to freeze the seven bills hastily pushed through by the old legislative council just before the handover. It said that to ensure economic development and the improvement of people's livelihood, thorough investigation and comprehensive consultation was needed before deciding on these matters.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said the proportional representation system planned for Hong Kong's legislative elections next year appeared to prevent the territory's most popular politicians from gaining any sizeable presence in the Legislative Council. Where was the "more democracy" for Hong Kong people promised by Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, the paper asked.
